The test image shows a tomato **leaf** with:
- Multiple dark brown/black irregular spots scattered across the surface
- A grayish-tan fuzzy/velvety area on the lower-right portion
- Spots are somewhat angular/irregular

The grayish fuzzy sporulation area and dark lesions suggest Gray_Mold (Botrytis) as the top candidate. Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The Gray_Mold reference shows large V-shaped tan blotches from leaf margins — quite different from the test image's discrete dark spots + fuzzy gray area.

**Re-analysis of the test image:**
- Multiple discrete dark/black angular spots scattered across the leaf
- A grayish-tan velvety/fuzzy growth area on the lower-right portion
- The leaf otherwise appears green
- The fuzzy grayish patch has the texture of fungal sporulation

This pattern — discrete dark necrotic spots combined with a velvety grayish-olive mold patch — is most consistent with **Leaf_Mold** (Passalora fulva). The grayish area matches the "olive-green to brown velvety mold on the lower surface" and the dark spots correspond to the upper surface lesions. The image appears to show the underside of the leaf where velvety sporulation is characteristic.
